headline: Roaches don't walk in. They arrive on the freight.
body_paragraph_1: German cockroaches don't overwinter outside. They live indoors year-round and arrive the way inventory does — in cardboard, produce crates, pallet wrap and returned equipment. In a warehouse or a retail back room, one contaminated shipment in July is a documented complaint in September.
body_paragraph_2: We treat the harborage, not the surface. Targeted gel and bait placements go into cracks, voids and equipment cavities, with monitors that tell us whether the population is falling between visits — and a written record for your audit file.
points_label: Three entry points we always check
point_1_body: Cardboard and pallets are the most common ride in.
point_2_body: Heat, water and food in one unventilated room.
point_3_body: Vending and appliance motors hold heat overnight.
note_body: Break down and remove cartons the day they land. Stacked cardboard in a back corridor is harborage, not storage — and it is the first thing an auditor photographs.
